transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-05
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Mark Reyes (CISO - Copperleaf), Lina Gomez (Head of Platform), Evan Chu (Infra), Rita Amadi (Legal)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
Copperleaf is evaluating Redwood for inference: decision drivers are SOC2/ISO coverage, SSO and SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs/retention, KMS/encryption options, and data residency. They want clear options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and a pilot path.

Topics: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption & KMS, data retention, deployment options, pricing for pilot

[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan at Redwood, AE. Quick round of intros?
[00:12] Mark Reyes: Mark here, CISO at Copperleaf. We own security sign-off.
[00:16] Lina Gomez: Lina, head of platform, I'll be driving the integration if we move forward.
[00:20] Evan Chu: Evan, infra. I'll be doing the tech work and any on-prem/VPC setup.
[00:24] Rita Amadi: Rita, legal. I'll flag any retention or contractual needs.
[00:29] Priya Raman: Hi all, Priya from Redwood SE, I'll be your technical lead. Nice to meet you.
[00:32] Jordan Ellis: Goal for today is to understand Copperleaf's security requirements and map Redwood's Hosted / Dedicated / Private options to those needs. Also to capture immediate blockers for procurement.

[03:05] Mark Reyes: To be blunt, we're most concerned about auditability and key control. We require SOC 2 Type II and alignment to an ISO 27k baseline, at minimum. We also need strict control over encryption keys — ideally customer-managed KMS or HSM.
[03:28] Jordan Ellis: Totally. We have customers on both models. For Hosted we can provide SOC 2 Type II, and BYOK via cloud KMS integrations in some cases. For Private deployments, you get full KMS control and on-prem HSM support.
[04:01] Lina Gomez: What's the difference in access controls? For role separation, like we need RBAC integrated with our existing SSO and groups from SAML assertions.
[04:18] Priya Raman: Our RBAC maps to SAML attributes. You can sync groups from your IdP and assign roles at token/route level; audit logs show which API key or user invoked a call. There's a couple of implementation details though.
[04:33] Evan Chu: Is that available in Hosted, or only Dedicated/Private? We have strict network egress rules for production keys.
[04:40] Priya Raman: Hosted supports SAML SSO for admin console and token scoping, but for full network isolation and private link you'd look at Dedicated or Private. Hosted does have VPC peering and some private link support depending on region. For guaranteed egress control you likely want Dedicated with private connectivity or Private deployment in your VPC.

[06:02] Mark Reyes: Audit logs: retention, tamper-evidence, and exportability are big. We need immutable logs retained for 2 years and export to our SIEM.
[06:20] Jordan Ellis: We can forward audit trails to customer-owned S3 or your SIEM. Retention windows are configurable; default is 90 days on Hosted unless you add extended retention. For Dedicated/Private you can set your own retention policy and host the logs in your environment.
[06:45] Rita Amadi: Any gap on SOC 2 vs ISO? We need to understand the controls mapping for our legal review.
[06:55] Priya Raman: We can share a SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO control mapping. There's also an optional attestation for encryption management. Jordan will send the SOC 2 report after the call.

[08:10] Lina Gomez: Data residency — we run across EMEA and NA and have customers whose data must not leave the region. Can Redwood pin model serving to regions?
[08:25] Jordan Ellis: Yes, we can pin workloads by region and have routing policies. For Hosted you can select region-specific endpoints; Dedicated gives you physical capacity in a region; Private is fully in your region.

[10:01] Evan Chu: For KMS: do you support external KMS such as AWS KMS with a CMK we control, or only Redwood-managed keys? And do you support HSM-backed keys for signing?
[10:18] Priya Raman: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has options for customer BYOK with cloud provider KMS in selected plans. HSM-backed keys on Private deployments are supported — we've done HSMs for FIPS/HSC requirements.
[11:00] Mark Reyes: What about request/response encryption in transit and at rest? We need TLS, mTLS for internal connections, and encryption of caches.
[11:15] Priya Raman: TLS everywhere, mTLS can be enabled on Private/Dedicated for internal node comms. KV cache is encrypted at rest; if you're using your KMS we'll manage keys per your policy.

[13:40] Lina Gomez: On RBAC, we want to restrict who can create model endpoints versus who can view metrics. How granular is your role model?
[13:51] Priya Raman: Roles are pretty granular — admin, devops, reader, auditor, model-deployer, etc. You can bind SAML groups to these roles. Also token scopes can restrict API usage to generation/embeddings only.

[15:22] Evan Chu: For Dedicated capacity, what's the isolation level? We're worried about noisy neighbors and noisy token usage.
[15:35] Jordan Ellis: Dedicated is GPU-level isolation; you get reserved pools assigned to your account. We also have autoscale policies and burst options, but performance SLOs are far more predictable than Hosted.

[17:05] Mark Reyes: Compliance question — do you provide penetration test results or facilitate pen tests? Some vendors block customer pen tests.
[17:18] Priya Raman: We share pentest summaries and will coordinate scoping for customer-led assessments in Private deployments. For Hosted we have a controlled process — third-party pentest reports are shared under NDA.

[18:55] Rita Amadi: For contracts we need specific clauses on data deletion and retention. If we require deletion of logs or data in 90 days, can Redwood comply? Also, how do you prove deletion?
[19:10] Jordan Ellis: We support configurable retention policies. For Hosted, deletion is handled via our data lifecycle APIs and we provide deletion receipts and audit entries. For Private, it's customer-controlled, so you can enforce deletion directly. We'll need legal to align on deletion SLAs.

[21:30] Lina Gomez: Can we get per-token cost estimates and how encryption/KMS choices affect cost? Trying to build a POC budget.
[21:45] Jordan Ellis: Encryption itself has small cost (KMS API calls), but the main cost is compute. Dedicated pilot pricing can be provided; we'll give a ballpark. Priya, we should model token loads for their prompt distribution.

[23:00] Priya Raman: Quick note on logging: we have three audit channels — event log (who did what), model run log (input/output metadata, not full content unless you opt in), and infra metrics. If you require full content logging for debugging that's opt-in and we can keep it customer-side.
[23:33] Evan Chu: We do not want model outputs stored in any vendor system for production traffic. Is that possible?
[23:40] Priya Raman: Yes. You can disable payload retention and route logs to your SIEM. For Hosted there's an option to disable content retention; for Dedicated/Private it's fully controllable. We'll capture that as a requirement.

[26:05] Mark Reyes: Regarding SSO: we use SAML with SCIM group provisioning. We want automated deprovisioning so that when someone is removed from AD they immediately lose access.
[26:20] Priya Raman: We support SCIM provisioning and deprovisioning with short token TTLs and OAauth/SAML for console access. Deprovisioning should be immediate within a minute or two depending on sync interval — we'll share the exact behavior.

[27:50] Jordan Ellis: Are there any blockers from a procurement or legal perspective we should know?
[28:00] Rita Amadi: We need the SOC 2 report, ISO mapping, liability caps, and deletion/retention SLAs in writing. Also network architecture for Private deployment and evidence of HSM/FIPS if we go that route.

[30:12] Priya Raman: For the technical deep dive we propose: run a short benchmark with a small sample workload on a staging endpoint, demonstrate SAML login + SCIM provisioning, and test log forwarding to your S3/SIEM. Would that cover your concerns?
[30:28] Lina Gomez: Yes that sounds right. Also want to validate latency SLOs for our 512-token use case.
[30:36] Evan Chu: And an architecture diagram showing how KMS keys are used for cache encryption and whether the KV cache can be kept in our VPC.

[33:00] Jordan Ellis: Great. I'll follow up with SOC2 and a high-level Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted comparison doc. Priya will coordinate the deep dive and bench.

[35:10] Mark Reyes: One last thing — audit log formats. We use JSON log lines with structured fields. Can you provide a sample schema?
[35:24] Priya Raman: Yes, we'll share a sample event schema and an example log pipeline to SIEM.

[37:40] Rita Amadi: Legal will likely ask about subprocessing and cross-border transfers. We'll want a list of subprocessors and data flow diagrams.
[37:52] Jordan Ellis: We'll include that in the packet.

[40:00] Short crosstalk / brief hold while attendees check notes
[41:05] Jordan Ellis: Recap of action items and next steps — Jordan send SOC2 & ISO mapping, Priya schedule deep dive and bench, Evan send infra diagram, Rita share retention policy, Redwood to produce pilot price ballpark.
[41:30] Mark Reyes: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[41:35] Lina Gomez: Thanks.
[41:38] Priya Raman: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites.

End of transcript.
